2607.07060.title: Complexity-Budgeted, Interaction-Aware Interpretable Model for Tabular Data
2607.07060.paper_summary: Inherently interpretable classifiers for tabular data typically rely on sparse features, rules, or patterns that users can inspect directly. The marginal feature-screening step common to these methods can discard variables whose predictive value emerges only through joint configurations with other variables. We present Interaction Aware Interpretable Machine Learning (IAIML), a framework that addresses this limitation through three coordinated mechanisms: adaptive per-feature discretization, finite-grid pairwise interaction scoring, and a partitioned explanation budget. Detected interactions are routed through one of two strategies: relaxing the screening filter so that interaction-supported variables enter the pattern search, or constructing explicit pair terms for a sparse downstream classifier. On a 40-dataset panel comprising 24 real-world tabular benchmarks and 16 synthetic interaction stress tests, evaluated under nested cross-validation, IAIML achieves mean AUC within 1.4 points of tuned gradient-boosted ensembles while requiring roughly 14--28 times fewer fitted explanation components. On datasets with strong pairwise interaction structure and low marginal signal, IAIML outperforms all baselines. Among compact interpretable methods, IAIML is comparable to RuleFit in AUC and component count and is less expensive to tune. EBM obtains a small but significant AUC advantage across the full panel, with a substantially larger lookup-table footprint. Performance degrades on datasets requiring higher-order interactions beyond the pairwise scope. Component-isolated ablations confirm that adaptive discretization and interaction-aware admission each contribute incrementally. These results support IAIML as a compact, interaction-aware framework appropriate for settings where bounded explanation size and controlled treatment of feature interactions are design requirements.
2607.07060.paper_summary_zh: 對於表格數據，本質上可解釋的分類器通常依賴於稀疏特徵、規則或用戶可以直接檢查的模式。這些方法中常見的邊際特徵篩選步驟可能會丟棄那些其預測價值僅通過與其他變數的聯合配置而顯現的變數。我們提出了互動感知可解釋機器學習（IAIML），這是一個通過三個協調機制來解決這一限制的框架：自適應每特徵離散化、有限網格成對互動評分和分區解釋預算。檢測到的互動通過兩種策略之一進行路由：放鬆篩選過濾器，使得支持互動的變數進入模式搜索，或為稀疏下游分類器構建顯式成對項。在一個包含24個真實世界表格基準和16個合成互動壓力測試的40數據集面板上，經過嵌套交叉驗證評估，IAIML在平均AUC上達到與調整後的梯度提升集成模型相差1.4點的範圍，同時需要大約14到28倍更少的擬合解釋組件。在具有強成對互動結構和低邊際信號的數據集上，IAIML的表現超過所有基準。在緊湊的可解釋方法中，IAIML在AUC和組件數量上與RuleFit相當，且調整成本更低。EBM在整個面板上獲得了小但顯著的AUC優勢，但查找表的佔用空間則大得多。在需要超出成對範疇的高階互動的數據集上，性能會下降。組件隔離的消融實驗確認自適應離散化和互動感知的接納各自都增量貢獻。這些結果支持IAIML作為一個緊湊的、互動感知的框架，適用於需要有限解釋大小和對特徵互動進行受控處理的設計要求的環境。
